gaps.title: Sharing flow (recipients, viewer/editor role, change and withdraw access) not shown
gaps.description: REQ-002 and REQ-003, as answered in DEC-001 and DEC-003, require the author to share a note with named team members as viewer or editor, with viewer as the default, and to change or withdraw access at any time. The capture shows a Share button with no target. It does not show how recipients are picked, how viewer or editor is chosen, who currently has access, or how access is changed or withdrawn.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing and per-person access are the core of two of the three approved requirements, and the mockup covers none of the steps after Share is pressed.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The sharing, access-listing and revocation behaviour cannot be specified or estimated, and the default viewer role could be applied inconsistently.
research_questions: How do established document-collaboration products (for example Google Docs, Microsoft 365, Notion) present per-person viewer/editor sharing, including the current access list and access removal?
What do accessible sharing dialogs need to do to meet WCAG 2.2 AA (focus management, role selection labels, status messages)?

gaps.title: Authorship of the single note per meeting is undefined
gaps.description: DEC-002 says a meeting has one note, REQ-001 says team members can write notes for each meeting, and REQ-003 says only the author can edit unless edit access is shared. It is not stated who becomes the author of a meeting's single note (for example whoever writes first, the meeting organiser, or someone else), or what other team members can do when the note already exists and they have not been given access.
gaps.why_it_matters: With one note per meeting and author-only editing, the choice of author decides who can write notes for a meeting at all. Read together, REQ-001 and REQ-003 can conflict.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Team members could be locked out of writing notes for meetings they attended, or two people could both expect to own the same note.

gaps.title: Visibility of a note before it is shared is not stated
gaps.description: CQ-004 asked whether an unshared note is private to its author or visible to the whole team. The answer recorded in DEC-004 covers how sharing works but does not say who can see a note that has not been shared with anyone, or whether team members who can see the meeting in the list can open its note.
gaps.why_it_matters: Meetings come from the team's shared calendar (DEC-002), so every team member may see every meeting in the list. Whether opening a meeting shows its note depends on default visibility, which is unresolved.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes could be exposed to team members the author never shared with, or hidden from people who expect to read them.

gaps.title: Editors' rights to delete or re-share a note are not stated
gaps.description: CQ-003 asked whether people with edit access can share, re-share or delete the note. The answer recorded in DEC-003 covers granting and withdrawing access by the author only. It does not say whether editors can share further, change other people's access, or delete the note, or whether the author can delete it.
gaps.why_it_matters: Deleting a meeting's only note (DEC-002) may destroy the sole record of that meeting, and editors re-sharing would weaken the author's control that REQ-003 sets up.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Delete and re-share permissions cannot be specified, risking irreversible loss of notes or access spreading without the author's consent.

gaps.title: Simultaneous editing by the author and editors is unaddressed
gaps.description: Because editors are now confirmed (DEC-003), the author and one or more editors may edit the same note at once. The inventory leaves open what happens when two people edit at the same time, and nothing in the capture shows presence, locking, conflict or stale-content states.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-004] 'What happens if two people edit at once?'

gaps.why_it_matters: There is one note per meeting and possibly several editors, so concurrent edits right after a meeting are likely.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: One person's save could silently overwrite another's notes.
research_questions: What conflict-handling approaches (last-write-wins with warning, optimistic locking, real-time co-editing) do shared note tools use for a single plain-text body, and what are their known failure modes?
How do products signal that a note was changed by someone else since it was opened?

gaps.title: Viewer (read-only) state and mid-edit access changes not shown
gaps.description: The capture shows only an editable Notes field with enabled Save and Share buttons. No read-only state for a viewer is shown, and it is not shown what someone sees without access. It is also not defined what happens to an editor's unsaved work if the author downgrades them to viewer or withdraws access while they are editing.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-001 'change or withdraw access at any time'

gaps.why_it_matters: Viewer is the default role (DEC-001), so most people opening a shared note will be viewers, and the author can change access at any time.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The viewer experience cannot be specified, and editors may lose work or keep editing after their access is withdrawn.
research_questions: How do collaborative editors handle a user whose edit permission is revoked while they have unsaved changes open?

gaps.title: Save behaviour, feedback and unsaved work not defined
gaps.description: The Save button has no target in the capture. It is not stated whether notes save only on Save or automatically, what success or failure feedback appears, or what happens to unsaved text when the user leaves the page, loses connection or the session ends.
gaps.why_it_matters: Writing notes (REQ-001) is the primary action, and notes are often typed live during a meeting, when losing text is costly.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users may lose notes without warning or be unsure whether their notes were saved.
research_questions: What are established practices for explicit save versus autosave in web note editors, including draft recovery after connection loss?
How should save success and failure be announced to meet WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages?

gaps.title: Effect of calendar changes and calendar outages on meetings and notes
gaps.description: Meetings come from the team's shared calendar (DEC-002). It is not defined what happens to a meeting's note when the calendar event is renamed, rescheduled, cancelled or deleted, where the attendee count shown on the meeting page comes from, or what users see when the calendar cannot be reached.
gaps.why_it_matters: Notes are attached to meetings the product does not own, so changes in the external calendar can orphan or mislabel notes.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes could disappear from the list, attach to the wrong meeting or become unreachable during a calendar outage.
research_questions: Which shared calendar platform is used (for example Google Calendar or Microsoft 365/Outlook), and how do its APIs signal event updates, cancellations and deletions?
What rate limits and availability constraints apply to reading team calendar events on that platform?

gaps.title: Team membership changes and author departure
gaps.description: Sharing is limited to named team members, and only the author can manage access (DEC-001). It is not defined what happens to a person's access when they leave the team, or who can manage or edit a note whose author leaves or whose account is removed.

evidence_refs.locator: REQ-001 ambiguity_notes 'Who counts as a team member'

gaps.why_it_matters: Only the author can grant or withdraw access, so a departed author leaves the meeting's only note with nobody able to manage it, and former team members might keep access.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes could become unmanageable, or people outside the team could keep reading them.

gaps.title: Meeting list contents, order, volume and empty/loading/error states
gaps.description: The list shows one meeting. It is not stated which calendar meetings appear (all, past only, attended only), their order, how a growing list is handled, or what is shown with no meetings, while loading or on failure. None of these states appear in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: The list is the only way into a meeting's note, and a shared team calendar can hold many events.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users may fail to find the meeting they need, and empty or failure cases would be built inconsistently.
research_questions: What defaults (date range, sort order, pagination or search) do meeting-notes tools linked to calendars use for long meeting lists?

gaps.title: Notification when a note is shared or access changes
gaps.description: It is not stated whether named team members are told when a note is shared with them or when their role changes or is withdrawn, through which channel, or what happens if delivery fails.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing is per named person, so recipients may not know that a note is available to them unless they are told.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Shared notes may go unread, or the notification scope may be decided late in development.
research_questions: What notification patterns (in-app, email) do collaborative document tools use for share and permission-change events?

gaps.title: Accessibility of the list and status feedback
gaps.description: The meetings table has an unlabelled action column and a repeated 'Open' link on each row. No status messages for Save or Share results are shown. Keyboard and focus behaviour for the sharing step is unobserved.
gaps.why_it_matters: Several identical 'Open' links in a list of meetings are hard to tell apart with assistive technology, and save and share outcomes are invisible without status messages.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The feature may fail WCAG 2.2 AA and need rework late in development.
research_questions: What do WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) and SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships require for repeated row-action links and unlabelled table columns?
What does WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages require for save and share confirmations?

gaps.title: Recovery of overwritten or deleted note content
gaps.description: It is not stated whether earlier versions of a note can be restored, or whether a deleted note or an accidental overwrite can be undone. No confirmation or undo state is shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-005] 'Can a save be undone or earlier versions restored?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Each meeting has a single note that editors can change, so one bad edit or delete affects the only record of that meeting.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Meeting records could be lost permanently, with no way to recover them.
research_questions: What version-history and restore patterns do shared note tools offer for single-document notes, and how long is history usually kept?

gaps.title: Note content format and limits
gaps.description: It is not stated whether notes are plain or rich text, whether attachments are allowed, or whether there is a length limit or other validation. The capture shows a plain text area with no limits indicated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Format and size decide how notes are stored, shown to viewers and edited by several people.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Format choices may be made by default during development and be costly to change later.

gaps.title: Traceability of edits and access changes
gaps.description: It is not stated whether the product must record who edited a note, or who granted, changed or withdrew access and when.
gaps.why_it_matters: With several editors on one note and access changing at any time, disputes about who changed what may need a record.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Edits and access changes cannot be traced if questions come up later.

assumptions.text: The SCR-002 meeting page shows the note as seen by someone with edit rights (the author or an editor), because Notes is editable and Save and Share are enabled.
assumptions.why: The capture shows a single state with no indication of the viewer's role.
assumptions.impact: Viewer and no-access states are treated as unobserved rather than contradicted.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm which role the mockup depicts.

assumptions.text: 'Named team members' in DEC-001 means sharing is limited to members of the same team, and people outside the team are out of scope.
assumptions.why: DEC-001 answered CQ-001 without explicitly addressing people outside the team.
assumptions.impact: No gap is raised about sharing outside the team; membership-change effects are raised in GAP-009.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm that notes can never be shared outside the team.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Default visibility of a note not yet shared is not answered by DEC-004 (see GAP-003).
Whether editors may delete or re-share, and who may delete a note, is not answered by DEC-003 (see GAP-004).
With one note per meeting (DEC-002), 'team members can write notes for each meeting' may conflict with author-only editing in REQ-003 (see GAP-002).
Author-only editing may conflict with REQ-001 given one note per meeting (DEC-002); authorship is undefined (see GAP-002).
